text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The major governing factions are to meet this week to discuss political processes in Latvia and prevent the cabinet from losing its stability, chairman of the Latvia's Way faction Andrejs Pantelejevs told a party conference on Saturday.
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele is likely to meet soon his Russian counterpart, Viktor Chernomyrdin, parliament chairman Alfred Chepanis announced after meeting Shkele Saturday.
- More than a half of Latvia's people distrust the courts, according to an opinion poll.
- Lattelekom has violated the human rights of its clients when publishing addresses in telephone directories without the client's consent.
- OSCE High Commissioner of the OSCE, Max Van der Stoel, arrived on a two day visit to Latvia.
- A revised credit rating for Riga city, made by Standard & Poor's, is due to be announced later this week.
- The association of Latvia's haulers, Latvijas Auto, held its annual meeting last Friday.
- Minister of Economics Guntars Krasts said at press conference on Friday that he will propose amendments to the statutes of the privatisation agency to choose directors in an open competition.
- Air Baltic announced plans to stop flying to Minsk from April 8 due to lower passenger numbers.
- Following the election of local governments, changes are likely to happen in the boards of both Riga and Liepaja ports.
